faq.q: What is the minimum investment for the Greece Golden Visa in 2026?
faq.a: As of November 2026, the minimum through real estate is €800,000 in Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and the large islands, and €400,000 in the rest of Greece, including Halkidiki, for one residential property of at least 120 m². A €250,000 threshold applies only to conversions of commercial buildings and to listed buildings. Our lawyer confirms the figures.

faq.q: Does property in Halkidiki qualify for the Greek Golden Visa?
faq.a: Yes. As of November 2026, Halkidiki is in the €400,000 zone under Law 5100/2024. A single residential property of at least 120 m², bought for €400,000 or more, can qualify, provided the other conditions are met, including no short-term letting. Our lawyer confirms each property before you commit.

faq.q: Does the Greece Golden Visa lead to citizenship?
faq.a: Not directly. The Golden Visa is a residence permit. Citizenship through naturalisation has separate conditions, including years of actual residence in Greece, knowledge of Greek and an exam. Holding a Golden Visa while living abroad does not usually count towards that time. Ask your lawyer if citizenship is your goal.

faq.q: Can my family be included in the Greece Golden Visa?
faq.a: Yes. As of November 2026, one qualifying investment normally covers your spouse or registered partner, your children under 21 and the parents of both spouses. Each receives their own residence permit, renewed together with the main applicant's. Our lawyer confirms who can be included in your case.

faq.q: Greece vs Portugal Golden Visa: what is the difference?
faq.a: For property buyers, the main difference is that Portugal stopped accepting real-estate purchases as a qualifying route for its golden visa in 2023, while Greece, as of November 2026, still does. Thresholds, conditions and timelines differ in both countries, so compare them with a lawyer before deciding.

intro: The Greece Golden Visa gives non-EU citizens a residence permit in return for an investment, most often the purchase of property. As of November 2026, Halkidiki is in the €400,000 zone: one residential property of at least 120 m² can qualify. This page explains the rules, the steps and what they mean for buying in Halkidiki, Northern Greece. All figures are as of November 2026 and to be confirmed by our lawyer. Rules change often, and this page is general information, not legal advice.
body:
What is the Greece Golden Visa?

The Golden Visa is a residence permit for non-EU citizens who make a qualifying investment in Greece. Through real estate, it is usually issued for five years and can be renewed as long as you keep the property and the conditions are still met. It lets you live in Greece and travel within the Schengen area under the rules for residents.

You do not have to live in Greece for a minimum number of days each year to keep it, but it does not give the right to work as an employee. EU citizens do not need a Golden Visa at all, because they can already live in Greece.

For many buyers it is a way to combine two goals: a home by the sea for their own use and the freedom to stay in Greece for as long as they like. Others use it as a secure base in Europe for the family, with the option to move later.

Minimum investment by area: why Halkidiki is in the €400,000 zone

Since Law 5100/2024, the minimum investment in property depends on the location. As of November 2026:

  • €800,000 in Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and the large islands
  • €400,000 in the rest of Greece, including Halkidiki
  • €250,000 only for converting a commercial building into a home, or for restoring a listed building

Halkidiki is a separate regional unit from Thessaloniki, so it falls in the €400,000 zone, while the start of the Kassandra peninsula is about an hour by car from Thessaloniki airport. For buyers who want the sea, road access and a lower threshold, this combination is worth a close look.

The threshold refers to the purchase price stated in the deed. Purchase costs come on top: as of November 2026, transfer tax of 3.09% on a resale, while VAT on new builds is suspended until 31/12/2026, plus lawyer, notary and land-registry fees that typically add several percent. Plan your total budget with these in mind.

Requirements: one residential property of 120 m² or more

In the €400,000 zone the main conditions, as of November 2026, are:

  • the investment must be in one residential property; several smaller properties cannot be combined to reach the threshold
  • the property must be at least 120 m²
  • the price must be paid in full through a Greek bank account
  • the property may not be used for short-term letting, such as holiday rentals, although long-term letting is allowed
  • applicants need, among other documents, health insurance that covers them in Greece and a clean criminal record

With older homes, the size in the title and the size built on site do not always match, and only legal, permitted space counts. Size, use and price are checked on the documents, so your lawyer confirms that each property qualifies before you sign. In Halkidiki, the homes that meet these conditions are mostly villas and larger houses.

The ban on short-term letting matters if you hoped to cover costs with holiday rentals. You can still let the home on a long-term lease, or keep it for your own family's use. Ask your lawyer how the rules apply before you choose between a holiday villa and a home you plan to let.

Family members and residence rights

One investment can cover your family. As of November 2026, to be confirmed by our lawyer, this normally includes your spouse or registered partner, your children under 21 and the parents of both spouses. Each family member receives their own residence permit, renewed together with yours.

Children can attend school in Greece while they hold the permit. Family members do not need to buy property of their own. If your children pass the age limit, your lawyer can explain the options available to them at renewal.

Golden Visa and Greek citizenship

The Golden Visa is residence, not citizenship. Greek citizenship through naturalisation has its own conditions, including years of actual residence in Greece, knowledge of the Greek language and culture, and an exam. Time spent holding a Golden Visa while living abroad does not usually count towards that. If citizenship is your long-term goal, discuss it with your lawyer before you buy.

Step by step: from property to residence permit

Before you start, gather the basics: valid passports for everyone applying, proof of family relationships, health insurance and the funds you will transfer through a Greek bank. Then the usual path is:

  • Choose a qualifying property and view it, in person or by video.
  • Get a Greek tax number (AFM) and open a Greek bank account.
  • Your lawyer checks the title, the permits, the size and that the property meets the Golden Visa conditions.
  • Sign the purchase deed at the notary and pay through the bank.
  • Register the deed at the land registry or cadastre.
  • Submit the residence application with the required documents, then give your biometrics in person.
  • Receive the residence permit, valid for five years and renewable while you keep the property.

Much of this can be done through your lawyer with a power of attorney, but you need to be in Greece for the biometrics. Processing times vary, so plan ahead.

At renewal, you show that you still own the property and that the conditions are still met. Your permit is linked to keeping the qualifying investment, so speak to your lawyer before you sell or transfer the home.

Golden Visa properties in Halkidiki

Below you will find homes in Halkidiki that may meet the €400,000 and 120 m² conditions, mainly villas and large houses, many with sea views and private pools. Every listing still needs your lawyer's confirmation before you rely on it for a Golden Visa.

Where to look depends on how you will use the home. Kassandra is closest to the airport and has the most services, which suits families who visit often. Sithonia offers privacy, pine forest and quiet coves. Nea Propontida and Polygyros have towns with year-round life, useful if you plan to live here for long periods.

A good approach is a short trip of a few days: we prepare a shortlist of qualifying homes in advance, you view them in person, and your lawyer starts the checks on the one you choose while you are still here.

Tell us your plans and budget. We arrange viewings in person or by video, work with your lawyer through the purchase and, once you own the home, can manage it while you are away.
